articleTitle: The Implementation of IoT Based Smart Refrigerator System
publicationTitle: 2018 2nd International Conference on Smart Sensors and Application (ICSSA)
abstract: Wasted food due to spoilage is a critical resource issue. Food waste or food loss is food that is discarded or lost uneaten. Currently, in the world, according to the Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations (FAO), consumers waste about 1.3 billion tons of food annually and consumers in rich countries waste about 222 million tons of food products. Once food products are purchased and set aside in a refrigerator, the users do not alert about their food items' expiration date and/or freshness unless they individually examine and track them. Moreover, for food products which are not labeled with an explicit expiration date may lead to significant food spoilage and additional expenditure for the users. However, with the latest trend technology of the Internet of Things (IoT), this problem can be resolved. Combining the idea of Internet of Things and smart kitchen evolution, the smart refrigerator system is developed. The system consists of three main parts which are sensing module, control module and transmission module. Sensing module consists of load cell and odour sensor while control module consists of Arduino UNO and power supply unit and last but not least, the transmission module consists of LCD module and Wi-Fi module. These modules work together to determine contents status inside the refrigerator and notify the user about the condition and quantity of the food via an SMS or an email.

articleTitle: IR 4.0 using IoT and LORAWAN to Accelerate Lentinula Edodes Growth
publicationTitle: 2018 2nd International Conference on Smart Sensors and Application (ICSSA)
abstract: High demand mushroom are lacking in the market. As such, production of mushroom needs to be expedite. Mushroom cultivation plays an important role to meet this high demand product. Mushroom cultivation is important due to its nutritional value, medicinal value, income generation and employment creation. Currently the mushroom cultivation are just being done in a very primitive way. Due to all these circumstances, it is crucial to upgrade the facilities to increase yield through optimum resources. One of the method is by controlling the climate to expedite and accelerate the growth in mushroom cultivation. Smart Mushroom Cultivation for mushroom cultivation is a project to address the automation in the production of expensive mushroom. The system developed is a smart system to manage the monitoring and control the devices such as sensors and actuators. The system utilizes IoT technology as part of IR 4.0 that consists of sensor technology with feedback system to optimize climate condition for maximum growth.

articleTitle: Design and Implementation of an IoT Based Monitoring System for Inland Vessels Using Multiple Sensors Network
publicationTitle: 2018 2nd International Conference on Smart Sensors and Application (ICSSA)
abstract: Multi sensor networks are now widely used in various security and surveillance applications. The paper includes designing and implementing a wireless sensor network with a real time web application for monitoring multiple ships to prevent catastrophic events due to overloading. The idea consists of four main parts: Detection Module, GPS tracker, communication system (NRF24L01+) and software application for web interface.

articleTitle: A Novel Approach for the Investigation of Flash Floods using Soil Flux and CO2: An Implementation of MLP with Less False Alarm Rate
publicationTitle: 2018 2nd International Conference on Smart Sensors and Application (ICSSA)
abstract: Extreme intensified flash floods and runoffs are the main root cause for the high number of casualties, properties and values belongings deficit within few seconds in so many countries. Flash floods are acknowledged as the most dangerous and unpredictable disasters in the whole world. Floods can be due to the heavy precipitation velocity, reservoir break, high oceanic waves at sea shore or snow melts briskly in oceans. Many techniques have been followed to investigate and forecast the flash floods on urgent basis. Almost dozens of sensors have been used to detect all the evaluation parameters concerned to the flash floods like upstream level, rainfall intensity, run-off magnitude, run-off speed, color of the water, precipitation velocity, pressure, temperature, wind speed, wave current pattern and cloud to ground (CG flashes). Ultrasonic and PIR sensors have also been used for this purpose. Transducers and sensing elements generate false alarms or missed information as well due to the inadequate algorithms. In our research we have proposed a novel approach analysis of soil flux depicting atmospheric carbon dioxide level as the plants take smaller amount of water from the soil due to the heightened levels of carbon dioxide. Due to this newly discovered phenomenon the soil is saturated briskly causes more floods and run-offs. In our research we have discarded the fake alerts and reduced the false alarms by using classifier multilayer perceptron (MLP). Experimental results demonstrated that MLP performed better than the other existing techniques.

articleTitle: Network Reconfiguration Using Modified Particle Swarm Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2018 2nd International Conference on Smart Sensors and Application (ICSSA)
abstract: This paper exhibits a successful strategy to ideally reconfigure a power distribution system. To locate the ideal blend of switches which outcomes with least power network losses in a distribution radial arrangement. Modified Particle Swarm Optimization (MPSO) technique is anticipated. MPSO is a modified Binary Particle Swarm Optimization (BPSO) with modification of particle velocity in search space. To exhibit the appropriateness of the suggested strategy relative investigation of MPSO with genetic algorithm (GA), ant-colony algorithm (ACA) and selective particle swarm optimizatio(SPSO) to reconfigure a power distribution system, under base case loading conditions, on IEEE 33 bus radial network is proposed. It is examined that MPSO performs better as compare to GA, ACA and SPSO in respective of significance of output, profile of voltage.

articleTitle: Implementation of operational amplifier for the designing of novel piezoresistive pressure sensor
publicationTitle: 2018 2nd International Conference on Smart Sensors and Application (ICSSA)
abstract: This work describes an idea of implementing operational amplifier for the designing of smart miniaturized piezoresistive pressure sensor for various applications. Boron doped p-type and phosphorus doped n-type piezoresistors are used as the sensing layers in order to detect the resistance change under an externally applied uniform pressure. A non-inverting operational amplifier (op-amp) has been used as the read-out circuitry of this novel piezoresistive pressure sensor which converts the resistance change in to the output voltage signal that is proportional to the input applied pressure. Intellisuite MEMS software is utilized for simulation of pressure sensor. Finite element method based Thermo-electro-mechanical (TEM) and Synple module is employed for structural and electrical analysis of the piezoresistive pressure sensor. The simulation result of this op-amp based piezoresistive pressure sensor using p-type piezoresistors has a sensitivity of approximately 156 mV/MPa whereas a sensitivity of 870 mV/MPa has been observed in case of using n-type piezoresistors.

articleTitle: Application of UAV and Low Power Wide Area Communication Technology for Monitoring of River Water Quality
publicationTitle: 2018 2nd International Conference on Smart Sensors and Application (ICSSA)
abstract: Pollution has been recognized as the major threat to sustainability of river in Malaysia. Some of the limitations of existing methods for river monitoring are cost of deployment, non-real-time monitoring, and low resolution both in time and space. To overcome these limitations, a smart river monitoring solution is proposed for river water quality in Malaysia. The proposed method incorporates unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV), internet of things (IoT), low power wide area (LPWA) and data analytic (DA). A setup of the proposed method and preliminary results are presented. The proposed method is expected to deliver an efficient and real-time solution for river monitoring in Malaysia.

articleTitle: Utilizing P-Type ILA in tuning Hybrid PID Controller for Double Link Flexible Robotic Manipulator
publicationTitle: 2018 2nd International Conference on Smart Sensors and Application (ICSSA)
abstract: The usage of robotic manipulator with multi-link structure has a great influence in most of the current industries. However, controlling the motion of multi-link manipulator has become a challenging task especially when the flexible structure is used. Currently, the system utilizes the complex mathematics to solve desired hub angle with the coupling effect and vibration in the system. Thus, this research aims to develop the controller for double-link flexible robotics manipulator (DLFRM) with the improvement on hub angle position and vibration suppression. The research utilized DLFRM modeling based on NARX model structure estimated by neural network. In the controllers' development, this research focuses on adaptive controller. PType iterative learning algorithm (ILA) control scheme is implemented to adapt the controller parameters to meet the desired performances when there are changes to the system. The hybrid PID-PID controller is developed for hub motion and end point vibration suppression of each link respectively. The controllers are tested in MATLAB/Simulink simulation environment. The performance of the controller is compared with the fixed hybrid PID-PID controller in term of input tracking and vibration suppression. The results indicate that the proposed controller is effective to move the double-link flexible robotic manipulator to the desired position with suppression of the vibration at the end of the double-link flexible robotic manipulator structure.

articleTitle: Double sampling control charts for monitoring the coefficient of variation
publicationTitle: 2018 2nd International Conference on Smart Sensors and Application (ICSSA)
abstract: The coefficient of variation (CV) is effective in monitoring the normalized measure of dispersion. It is extensively applied in the situations where the mean and standard deviation are not constant for all time. In this paper, the double sampling control chart is proposed to monitor the CV (abbreviated as DS-γ). Two optimization algorithms of the DS-γ chart are developed, i.e., to minimize (i) the average number of observations to signal (ANOS) when the shift size to be known a priori and (ii) the expected average number of observations to signal (EANOS) when the shift size is unknown. The proposed chart's performance is then compared with the standard CV chart. The results show the proposed DS-γ chart significantly outperforms the standard CV chart in the detection of all ranges of shifts in the CV.

Author Keywords: Average number of observations to signal
Expected average number of observations to signal

articleTitle: Smart Monitoring and Auto-Neutralization of pH of Alkaline Liquids in Process Industries
publicationTitle: 2018 2nd International Conference on Smart Sensors and Application (ICSSA)
abstract: In recent years, the use of wireless technology is widely encouraged in many industrial applications. The use of wireless technology has quite a few benefits when it is used in industries. In some of these industries, critical processes and hazardous environment are now physically managed by the employees. Especially in Nuclear power plants where presence of employees is required at the specific sites. This is seen as a threat for human life due to the hazardous environment like nuclear radiation. Even-though safety precautions are followed by the concerned employees, the threat remains same. This paper proposes a wireless smart monitoring and automatic neutralization process of liquid pH in process industries. This eliminates the need of physical presence of employees in the hazardous process area, thus reducing the occupational health and safety related issues.

articleTitle: Analysis on Tuning Strategy of pH Control Process in Paper Industries
publicationTitle: 2018 2nd International Conference on Smart Sensors and Application (ICSSA)
abstract: In modern days, the pH level maintaining the process solution present in the cylindrical tank is an essential factor in paper and chemical industries. The main thing is to keep, the pH value of the solution in the neutral range, proper controlled mixing of acid and base solutions is needed. So in this paper, such a control problem has been addressed using the conventional PID controller with different tuning methods along with advanced controllers like Fractional Order PID controller (FOPID), Neural controller and Internal Model Controller (IMC). In addition to that, the FOPID controller with different tuning methods has implemented for pH level control. The system performance has analyzed with the help of MATLAB simulation. By comparing the responses of different controllers, the suitable controller has adopted for maintaining the pH level.

articleTitle: ElectriCare – Care, Protection & Automation
publicationTitle: 2018 2nd International Conference on Smart Sensors and Application (ICSSA)
abstract: With emerging advancements of technology, we can observe the increasing number of automation technologies that has made life easier and simpler in all aspects. With a swift upturn in the number of internet users over the preceding span has made internet turn into a gist of life. The said automation technology i.e. IoT (Internet of Things), has taken us to anew world of automation. In this new era of Internet Revolution, where we tend to discover approaches to make things inside the range of our fingertips, prompted the advancement of Home Automation Systems. Controlling and monitoring the home has never been so easyand secure until science made thispossible. In this paper, we present a solution, ElectriCare, which is an IoT based home automation and monitoring system that provides the ability to control and conserve electricity with the sense of intelligence. This intelligence feature helps us to design a system that lets user in control of their electronics and allowing them to also automate their liveswith the help of on-board sensors. It uses smart phone application to control the appliances via the internet from anyplace round the globe. It uses Wi-Fi to communicatewith the microcontroller to control as well as it creates a log of the electricity consumption to help save energy as it is destined to conserve the electric and human power.

articleTitle: Wireless IMU: A Wearable Smart Sensor for Disability Rehabilitation Training
publicationTitle: 2018 2nd International Conference on Smart Sensors and Application (ICSSA)
abstract: We proposed a wearable wireless gait sensing system for the home monitoring of specific symptoms of gait disabled people. The wearable wireless system is combination of sensory and data acquisition system. Sensory part consists of inertial measurement unit (IMU), atmega328 controller, and a Bluetooth module. The software is basically an application data acquisition and processing system for tablet or PC. The software is embedded with recognition algorithms which use fusion of raw signals from IMU. The system provides a robust and reliable detection of the abnormal gait which is very common to post stroke people which causing abnormality of their movement. The proposed system will provide the rehabilitation training for the post stroke people by playing the virtual game therapy to recover from their movement problem.

articleTitle: Bird Counting and Climate Monitoring using LoRaWAN in Swiftlet Farming for IR4.0 Applications
publicationTitle: 2018 2nd International Conference on Smart Sensors and Application (ICSSA)
abstract: In recent years, the edible swiftlet bird nest is a growing industry in Malaysia. Farmers simulate the swiftlet's habitat in buildings widely known as swiftlet bird houses. The suitability of the environment or condition in these houses are largely unknown as there seems very little research effort is done in this newly formed industry. This paper presents a realtime environment monitoring and control system utilizing wireless sensor network such as LoRaWAN. The monitored sensor data include humidity, temperature, oxygen, and luminance were recorded in a swiftlet bird house in Terengganu. Ambient and indoor humidity, temperature and oxygen level variations were also investigated. Internet of Things (IoT) and video analytics which are part of Industrial Revolution 4.0 (IR 4.0) technologies are used in this project. The studies have shown that the combination of suitable temperature, humidity and oxygen inside the swiftlet bird house will increase the amount of edible bird nest.

articleTitle: Dynamic Resource Allocation Strategy for Low Cost Smart Parking System
publicationTitle: 2018 2nd International Conference on Smart Sensors and Application (ICSSA)
abstract: This paper introduces a new practical solution to overcome limited resources associated with high customer demand issues such as limited availability of parking space in building complex. In the globalization era, where the urban population is increasing, more cars are being used thus increasing the demand for parking space and contributing to traffic congestion. In general, everyone has his/her own intention for going to a building complex and based on that, he/she can estimate the amount of time to be spent there. The concept introduced categorized the parking space into several categories based on the estimated time spent at the building complex. By implementing this concept within the smart system, we will be able to allocate resources dynamically using the scheduling system of Google maps. With the integration of the Internet of Thing (IoT), the smart parking guidance system (SPGS) can allocate the parking space even when it is not available prior to the user entering the parking lot since the system knows when it is going to be vacant next so the system can match it with the estimated time of arrival of the user.

articleTitle: Development of Stereo Matching Algorithm Based on Guided Filter
publicationTitle: 2018 2nd International Conference on Smart Sensors and Application (ICSSA)
abstract: This article presents a new stereo matching algorithm to estimate a disparity or depth map. This map contains depth information from stereo matching process. Commonly, the region of low texture area is the most difficult and challenging area for matching process to get accurate result. Thus, the proposed work in this article uses an edge preserving filter to decrease the noise and surge the accuracy on this region. The filter is known as Guided Filter (GF). The GF is robust on the low texture area with high contrast and brightness. It is also capable to sharpen and decrease the noise on the filtered images. From the standard dataset for stereo evaluation of the Middlebury, the propose framework gains precise results and perform better than some of established algorithms in the evaluated database.

articleTitle: Temperature Distribution Study for Malaysia Broiler House
publicationTitle: 2018 2nd International Conference on Smart Sensors and Application (ICSSA)
abstract: Temperature control in broiler house is one of a crucial factor to make the broilers grow healthy. Utilization of heat source such as light bulb to provide heat and maintain optimum temperature in the broiler house becomes popular among the farmers in Malaysia. However, some heat sources consume enormous energy where some bulbs produce more light than heat. Maintaining the heat within the broiler house remains a challenge as some heat sources produces heat that burn the chicks. Thus, energy usage of the bulb is one of the biggest concerns of the local broiler farmers because it increases the operational cost of broiler house. This paper presents the study of temperature distribution of the common types of bulbs available in Malaysia that are used in farming. The height of the bulb installed in the barn is studied as well. The experimental model mimicking broiler house was built (10 ft ×10 ft) with 8 temperature sensors placed at different positions inside the experimental model. Four common light bulbs used by Malaysia farmers have been tested and the temperature distribution of all tested bulbs are discussed. Among these four bulbs, the Philips 150 W infrared bulb covers wider area with consistent temperature within the experimental model.

articleTitle: Design and Implementation of an Automated Multi-Functional Attendance System with Real Time Web Visualization
publicationTitle: 2018 2nd International Conference on Smart Sensors and Application (ICSSA)
abstract: In the recent times the security crisis is on the rise, safety and security of not only humans but also confidential information has become a big concern for everyone. An automated web based multifunctional attendance system is built to keep track of people getting in and out of an institution, it is an attendance system which ensures that unexpected people do not have access to important information. This system has RFID entry, finger print scanning and real time facial recognition all together to ensure full security, the data of attendance is available on the website for a better visualization. It eliminates the flaw of the traditional attendance system which can ensure neither proper security nor proper attendance. This system mitigates the present security concerns.

articleTitle: Modeling of a Flexible Beam System using NARMAX Model integrated with Multi-Objective optimization Differential Evolution
publicationTitle: 2018 2nd International Conference on Smart Sensors and Application (ICSSA)
abstract: Modeling a dynamic system such as a flexible beam system without knowing the physical equations involved is a challenging task. An accurate model representing the system is needed for more efficient controller design. This paper presents the identification of a flexible beam system using Nonlinear Auto- Regressive Moving Average with eXogenous input (NARMAX) model integrating with Multi-Objective optimization Differential Evolution (MOODE) algorithm. This proposed algorithm called MOODE-NARMAX is applied to minimize two objective functions; the model complexity and the mean square error between actual and predicted outputs. The system identification procedures were followed for identifying the flexible beam system. Model validity tests were applied to the set of solutions called the Pareto-optimal set that was generated from the proposed algorithm to select an optimal model. Using the input and output experimental data of the rig, the simulation results show that the MOODE-NARMAX algorithm is able to produce an adequate and optimal model for the flexible beam system and therefore could be used as an alternative to identify an adequate and parsimonious model for the system.

articleTitle: ICSSA 2018 keynote
publicationTitle: 2018 2nd International Conference on Smart Sensors and Application (ICSSA)
abstract: Provides an abstract of the keynote presentation and may include a brief professional biography of the presenter. The complete presentation was not made available for publication as part of the conference proceedings.

articleTitle: Version for Modified Nodal Array Approach in Foot Plantar Pressure Measurement System
publicationTitle: 2018 2nd International Conference on Smart Sensors and Application (ICSSA)
abstract: In this paper, we constructed and compared four version of varying mechanism for modifiedNodal Array Approach (NAA) in foot plantar pressure measurement system. In order to achieve NAA goals in having low circuit complexity while maintaining simple reading and solving algorithm, the varying mechanism part needs to be designed carefully by considering the factors such as low in sensor calculation error, component usage and complexity as well as algorithm size. 31 experiment conditions has been tested on these readout circuits with different varying mechanism where the results was presented, analyzed and discussed. A conclusion has been made wherethe Switch version has been selected to be the most suitable varying mechanism for the modified NAA readout circuit.

articleTitle: Investigation of Radial Piezoelectric-Magnetic Fan for Electronic Cooling System
publicationTitle: 2018 2nd International Conference on Smart Sensors and Application (ICSSA)
abstract: Application of piezoelectric fan in cooling electronic devices has been proven that it is more efficient that natural convection and has high potential to replace existing rotary fan. Radial Piezoelectric-Magnetic fan (RPMF) has introduced the integration of piezo-magnet to reduce power consumption and radial orientation to increase the repulsive magnetic force to be distributed to other adjacent magnetic fans. In this study 4 magnetic fans were activated by a single piezoelectric fan. All fans were vibrating but in reducing amplitude as the passive fans are located farther from the driving fan (piezo fan). The distribution of repulsive magnetic fan is different in array and radial orientation. The radial orientation has a better distribution angle compared to array orientation.

articleTitle: The Petrophysical Relationship between the Dielectric Permittivity and Water Content of Peat Soil Moisture Measurements
publicationTitle: 2018 2nd International Conference on Smart Sensors and Application (ICSSA)
abstract: Understanding the water content patterns of soil is important in agriculture, ecosystems, and in terms of the quality of the soil, especially in peat soil. To determine the water content of peat soil, an appropriate site-specific petrophysical relationship is needed. Although a few petrophysical relationships have been established, such as the Topp equation, which is commonly used by researchers to determine the water content, the signal tends to deviate when applied in organic soils. Hence, this study aims to determine a mathematical model for the site-specific petrophysical relationship between the dielectric permittivity and the soil moisture of peat soil. Samples of peat soil were taken for laboratory measurement. A two-dimensional adjusted parallel plate capacitor was designed and fabricated for determination of the dielectric permittivity. The oven drying process was conducted for estimation of the water content. A model fitting of the relationship between the dielectric permittivity and water content was proposed, and the results indicate that a two-dimensional adjustable soil cylindrical capacitor can be used to construct a good relationship between the dielectric permittivity and the water content. Hence this appropriate site specific petrophysical relationship can be used by the GPR to determine the water content of the peat soil. Linear and polynomial models were adjusted for the peat soil in respect of the dielectric permittivity and water content. Through verifying this site-specific petrophysical relationship using GPR with a frequency of 250MHz, the adjusted linear and polynomial models provide sufficient accuracy to determine the water content of peat soil.

articleTitle: Review of Taxi Cab Service Optimization in Petaling Jaya, Malaysia Based On Demand and Offer
publicationTitle: 2018 2nd International Conference on Smart Sensors and Application (ICSSA)
abstract: In this paper, several approaches were evaluated to assign taxi cabs to passenger's demand in the Universiti Malaya Medical Centre (UMMC) vicinity area. UMMC located in the heart of Petaling Jaya, Selangor. The main purpose of this paper covers two aspects; to identify the efficient solution for taxi cab assignments to pick up the passengers by minimizing the travelling distance and time taken and taxi cab assignment strategy. The calculation method to measure the taxi cab distance to the passengers was based on two methods; Euclidean distance and shortest path algorithm based on GPS-based routing. For the taxi cab assignment strategy, two algorithms were used; the Greedy Algorithm and Hungarian Algorithm. The Greedy Algorithm is based on nearest vehicles to the passenger while the Hungarian Algorithm is based on matrix calculation of the requested calls and number of available taxi cabs. The combination of two distance calculation and two vehicles assignment produced four possible approaches. These four approaches were further evaluated in three different scenarios using a simulator.

articleTitle: Simultaneous Heat and Mass Transfer in Kek Lapis Sarawak Baking
publicationTitle: 2018 2nd International Conference on Smart Sensors and Application (ICSSA)
abstract: Kek Lapis Sarawak is a specialty of Sarawak. Nowadays, energy becomes a global issue and there is call to minimize energy consumption for a better tomorrow. In cake industry, the use of oven in baking process contributes to the major energy consumption. This research aims to optimize the baking process for an efficient energy consumption. Therefore, it is very important to investigate the relationship between baking temperature, time and cake quality so that the baking process can be optimized. Kek Lapis Sarawak baking process has been modelled and simulate using finite element method (FEM). Then, results from the model was validated with experiment. As a result, similar model of the Kek Lapis Sarawak baking process has been developed. The finding shows interdependent relationship between porosity, thermal conductivity and moisture content where higher porosity that can lead to poor thermal conductivity.

articleTitle: Harvesting Sustainable Energy from Salt Water: Part I – Effect of Types of Electrodes
publicationTitle: 2018 2nd International Conference on Smart Sensors and Application (ICSSA)
abstract: In the last decade solar energy has been identified as one of the main alternative sources of energy with great potential to satisfy the world's energy needs. Unfortunately, the high capital cost of photovoltaic (PV) systems has prevented the widespread adoption of this kind of technology in developing countries. A new promising renewable energy source known as blue energy that takes advantage of the conductive nature of salt water has kept the researchers and engineers worldwide busiest at work. However, very limited research has been carried out in Malaysia in terms of harnessing sustainable energy from salt water and the findings were not well documented. The main objective of this research project is to produce a cost-effective new ilumination technology powered by salt water for rural and remote communities in Malaysia as well as worldwide. To realize this mission, a thorough investigation on the factors affecting the performance of the salwater energy product must undertaken. This paper particularly discusses the effect of electrode's combinations, number of cells and the durability of the electrodes after prolonged submergence in saltwater solution. The findings obtained from these experiments will be used to design a prototype of the illumination technology for further product development.

articleTitle: Hybrid Power Supply System for Telecommunication Base Station
publicationTitle: 2018 2nd International Conference on Smart Sensors and Application (ICSSA)
abstract: This research paper presents the results of the implementation of solar hybrid power supply system at telecommunication base tower to reduce the fuel consumption at rural area. An adequate strategy has been developed that incorporate solar energy as a primarypower source and diesel generator as well as battery for backup power system. The study, which resulted in the minimum cost of fuel consumption and reduces operational cost is defined formulated. An analysis is also performed to evaluate the impact of solar panel and the effectiveness of the implementation at the off-grid site.

articleTitle: Military Uniform for Health Analytics for Field Intelligent Zone (MUHAFIZ) Protecting the ones that protect our land
publicationTitle: 2018 2nd International Conference on Smart Sensors and Application (ICSSA)
abstract: Armed forces are one of the most integral part of any country. Being in one of the most hostile and critical environment they constantly face both mental and physical challenges. Those soldiers are always at risk and when met with an unfortunate incident, they remain isolated from instantaneous medical help. In these situations, it is essential to monitor and track each individual in real-time so that it can be concluded from the accumulated data as which individual requires immediate medical help and which one performs exceptionally well that can be considered a preferred candidate for the up-coming specific missions. In this paper, we present the system of an embedded next generation tactical suit designed for monitoring health statistics/analytics of an armed personnel. The suit has an onboard integrated CPU that extracts data from multiple sensors and send this information using LoRaWAN (Long Range Wide Area Network) technology. This information is recorded into the database, according to each suit and can be viewed in real-time or with respective to each individual. The paper also discusses the advantages of using LoRa and describes the system architecture and the working of the suit.

Author Keywords: Suit, Jacket, Data Analytics, Health Statistics, Health Monitoring, Vital Signs, Military Application Emergency Response

articleTitle: Girth Measuring Device and System based on RFID/WSN Technology in Rubber Plantation: A Preliminary Data
publicationTitle: 2018 2nd International Conference on Smart Sensors and Application (ICSSA)
abstract: This paper describes the performance of an automated girth measuring device (GMD) using RFID/WSN technologies in monitoring tree circumference and population in rubber plantations. For this study, GMDs together with RFID tags were installed on rubber tree trunks at different stages of the rubber tree development. Information from both devices were gathered wirelessly by a reader before being transferred to the Rubber Management System (RMS) software for data analysis. In addition, GMD performance was compared with data manually measured by using the conventional system and its reading distance was also determined. The GMD measurements are statistically the same as the manual measurements (P > 0.05) with an average error value of below 0.1cm. There is a decreasing pattern of error values as the girth of the trunk increases. Meanwhile, an average read range radius of 85 metres was recorded.

articleTitle: Terrestrial Land Rover with Dedicated Website
publicationTitle: 2018 2nd International Conference on Smart Sensors and Application (ICSSA)
abstract: Surveillance and rescue rover has become a common term of this decade, all the existing rover is trying to provide the best surveillance through its features, Terrestrial Land Rover with Dedicated Website is a rover that has been designed with features that can provide a better visualization of the region it goes through with the help of a dedicated website. The main goal of this project is to design a surveillance rover that provides maximum assistance to the rescue party by providing a clear view of the region. This rover has been implemented using a raspberry pi interface which provides with fast processing of data. Terrestrial Land Rover with Dedicated Website has been built to ensure quick and efficient rescue system, we do not want to lose more lives.

articleTitle: Reference Evapotranspiration Estimation in Tropical Region using Penman-Monteith Equation and Evolutionary Computation
publicationTitle: 2018 2nd International Conference on Smart Sensors and Application (ICSSA)
abstract: Evapotranspiration is the combined processes of evaporation and transpiration that give means the process of water loss to the atmosphere. Reference evapotranspiration (ETo) estimation is of importance in planning and management of water resource systems for irrigation purposes. Due to its importance, the accurate modeling of ETo is of vital importance to estimate crop water requirement and its availability. This study presents a system identification and differential evolution approach, for modeling daily and monthly ETo in peninsular of Malaysia, for a month period August 2011. The data set comprising dry bulb temperature, relative humidity, wind speed, and solar radiation was utilized for estimating ETo using FAO-56 Penman-Monteith equation as the reference. The modeling results were analyzed and compared with the traditional Penman Monteith (PM) method. Based on the analyses, the approach used was found that the models of ETo is adequate, understandable, and suited to estimate the dynamics of the evapotranspiration process. The performance of the model is comparable with that of the PM method.

articleTitle: Mass Rapid Transit Elevated Stations as Solar Electricity Generation
publicationTitle: 2018 2nd International Conference on Smart Sensors and Application (ICSSA)
abstract: This paper aims to utilize Mass Rapid Transit (MRT) Elevated stations roof area in m2 as solar electricity generation and parallelly to contribute energy by compensates energy demand challenges encountered by energy service providers with year to year demand increases. The geography of Malaysia, which is part of mainland of Southeast Asia located near to Equator with an annual average of solar irradiance 4.9 kWh/m2/day, ambient temperature 25.53 °C, wind speed 2.24 m/s and air mass 1.5 which are favorable parameters for the optimal solar power generation. Total of 24 elevated stations that were built for Klang Valley MRT line 1. Those station roofs are just built as shelters for stations which can be utilized by installing solar panels to compensate energy demand to the nation and indirectly revenBe collection to the stakeholders. The key challenges in this research were identification of the best optimal solar panels and the inverters within lower cost with optimal outputs and ROI (Return on Investment).
